overview.text: Mehmet Oz, commonly known as Dr. Oz, is an American cardiothoracic surgeon and television personality whose public profile connects medicine, mass media, and politics. A Columbia University profile describes him as a cardiac surgeon and professor who brought health education to television: he appeared regularly on The Oprah Winfrey Show before hosting his own health-focused daytime program. In 2022, he ran as the Republican candidate for a Pennsylvania U.S. Senate seat; Federal Election Commission results show Democrat John Fetterman won the general election. The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services now lists Oz as its administrator. His career is distinctive for carrying a physician’s celebrity platform into electoral politics and leadership of a major federal health agency.

key_facts.text: Oz earned an undergraduate degree at Harvard and a joint MD and MBA from the University of Pennsylvania and Wharton, according to his CMS biography.
A 2009 Columbia Magazine profile identifies Oz as a cardiac surgeon and professor at Columbia, as well as an attending surgeon at New York-Presbyterian at that time.
The Columbia profile says Oprah Winfrey began inviting Oz onto her show in 2004; he became a regular guest before hosting his own health-focused program.
In the 2022 Pennsylvania Senate general election, Republican Mehmet Oz received 46.27% of the vote, while Democrat John Fetterman received 51.17%.
As of September 24, 2026, the CMS website lists Oz as Administrator of the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services.
